raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43864

An audio request sent to a model whose multimodal processor defines an audio token but has no audio tower - e.g. `gemma-4-31B-it`, a non-audio variant of the Gemma 4 family whose `config.json` ships `audio_config: null` - is not rejected at the API layer. It reaches the scheduler, where `get_audio_feature()` raises inside `model.forward`, and the whole scheduler process dies.

Two underlying problems, both fixed here:

1. Request validation only checks `is_multimodal`, not per-modality capability, so the audio request passes tokenization/dispatch and fails deep in the scheduler, killing the scheduler process.
2. `ModelConfig.is_audio_understandable_model` used `hasattr(hf_config, "audio_config")`. Because the config key is present with a `null` value, `hasattr` is `True` even though no audio tower exists, and the model is misreported as audio-capable (`/get_model_info`: `has_audio_understanding: true` for `gemma-4-31B-it`).

Scope:

- The crash (problem 1) affects only models whose processor defines an audio token while the model has no audio tower. For all other models the audio never reaches the scheduler: models whose processor defines no audio token drop it in the processor, and text-only LLMs have no multimodal processor at all.
- The misreport (problem 2) is a config-level issue: it affects any model whose `config.json` carries `audio_config` with a `null` value.
- Existing behavior is otherwise unchanged: for models whose processor defines no audio token, requests are handled exactly as before (verified on `glm-5.3-flash`, see Production verification). The only intentional exception is the corner case noted under Limitations.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`: `is_audio_understandable_model` now requires `audio_config` to be present and non-`None` (top-level and under `thinker_config`) instead of `hasattr`. This makes the capability flag - and the `/get_model_info` report - correct for models with a `null` audio config.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py` (`_tokenize_one_request`): reject with a per-request error when a request carries audio data, the model's multimodal processor defines an audio token, and `is_audio_understandable_model` is `False`, return 400 with :

  ```
  Audio inputs are not supported by <served_model_name>
  ```
  Limitations:
  - Audio only; the same shape of problem could exist for other modalities but is out of scope here.
  - Corner case : on the native `/generate` path, a request that passes valid `audio_data` for a model whose processor defines an audio token but which has no audio tower, while the prompt carries no audio placeholder, used to succeed (the base processor drops the surplus audio with a warning); it is now rejected with the same 400 error. The OpenAI path is unaffected - it always inserts the placeholder, and those requests previously crashed the scheduler. We keep the broader guard because an explicit error is preferable to silently discarding user-provided audio.

## Accuracy Tests

No model output path is changed (the guard rejects requests that would otherwise crash the engine; the config-flag change only corrects a misreported capability), and existing behavior for models whose processor defines no audio token is preserved. 

Verified on `gemma-4-31B-it` (4x H20): an audio request now returns a clean per-request error instead of killing the scheduler, and the engine keeps serving:

```json
{"object":"error","message":"Audio inputs are not supported by gemma-4-31B-it","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

Existing behavior also verified on `glm-5.3-flash` (whose processor defines no audio token): an audio request still returns 200 exactly as before this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable - no change to the forward path; the only addition is a lightweight per-request validation at tokenization time.


## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) - N/A: the Gemma 4 cookbook page already documents which variants support audio; no doc change needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) - N/A: no model-output or performance change (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""
+Unit tests for early audio rejection in TokenizerManager._tokenize_one_request.
+
+A request carrying audio for a model that declares audio support but has no
+audio tower (e.g. a non-audio variant of a multimodal family such as
+gemma-4-31B-it) must be rejected with a per-request error at tokenization
+time. Without the guard, the audio items reach the scheduler, where
+get_audio_feature() raises inside model.forward and kills the scheduler
+process.
+
+Covers:
+  - audio + audio-declaring model without an audio tower -> ValueError
+    naming the served model, raised before validation/dispatch
+  - empty audio payloads (None, [], [None], [[None]]) are not rejected
+  - audio + audio-capable model proceeds
+  - models whose processor does not declare audio (or have no processor)
+    keep their existing behavior and are not rejected
+  - the --language-model-only message takes precedence over the audio one
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, Mock, patch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import GenerateReqInput  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager import TokenizerManager  # noqa: E402
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _make_mm_processor(declares_audio: bool):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        mm_tokens=SimpleNamespace(audio_token="<|audio|>" if declares_audio else None),
+        prefer_tokenized_input=False,
+    )
+
+
+def _make_tm(declares_audio: bool = True) -> TokenizerManager:
+    tm = TokenizerManager.__new__(TokenizerManager)
+    tm.model_config = MagicMock()
+    tm.model_config.is_audio_understandable_model = False
+    tm.model_config.hf_config.architectures = ["Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration"]
+    tm.served_model_name = "test-model"
+    tm.max_req_input_len = 8192
+    tm.mm_processor = _make_mm_processor(declares_audio)
+    return tm
+
+
+def _make_request(audio_data):
+    return GenerateReqInput(input_ids=[1, 2, 3], audio_data=audio_data)
+
+
+def _run_tokenize(tm, request, language_model_only=False):
+    async def drive():
+        with patch(
+            "sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager.get_disagg",
+            return_value=SimpleNamespace(
+                language_model_only=language_model_only,
+                language_only=False,
+                encoder_transfer_backend="zmq_to_scheduler",
+            ),
+        ):
+            return await tm._tokenize_one_request(request)
+
+    return asyncio.run(drive())
+
+
+def _stub_pipeline_past_guard(tm: TokenizerManager, sentinel: object) -> None:
+    """Stub the pipeline past the audio guard so these tests assert on the
+    guard boundary without a live runtime context (mm limits and the mm
+    processor pipeline need scheduler-side context bags)."""
+    tm._validate_mm_limits = Mock()
+    tm._normalize_mm_content_hashes = Mock()
+    tm._validate_one_request = Mock()
+    tm._create_tokenized_object = Mock(return_value=sentinel)
+    if tm.mm_processor is not None:
+        tm.mm_processor.process_mm_data_async = AsyncMock(return_value=None)
+
+
+class TestAudioRejectionInTokenizeOneRequest(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_audio_rejected_with_served_model_name(self):
+        tm = _make_tm()
+        tm._validate_one_request = Mock()
+        request = _make_request(["x.wav"])
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
+            ValueError, "Audio inputs are not supported by test-model"
+        ):
+            _run_tokenize(tm, request)
+
+        tm._validate_one_request.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_empty_audio_payload_is_not_rejected(self):
+        """Empty audio payloads carry no audio; an is-not-None check would
+        wrongly reject them (batch normalization fills audio_data with
+        [None] * n for text-only batches)."""
+        for payload in (None, [], [None], [[None]]):
+            with self.subTest(payload=payload):
+                tm = _make_tm()
+                sentinel = object()
+                _stub_pipeline_past_guard(tm, sentinel)
+
+                self.assertIs(_run_tokenize(tm, _make_request(payload)), sentinel)
+
+    def test_audio_allowed_for_audio_capable_model(self):
+        tm = _make_tm()
+        tm.model_config.is_audio_understandable_model = True
+        sentinel = object()
+        _stub_pipeline_past_guard(tm, sentinel)
+
+        self.assertIs(_run_tokenize(tm, _make_request(["x.wav"])), sentinel)
+
+    def test_audio_not_rejected_when_audio_is_not_declared(self):
+        """Processors without an audio token never carry audio to the
+        scheduler (the base processor drops it), so such models keep their
+        existing behavior: the request still goes through the multimodal
+        path and is not rejected. Text-only models without a multimodal
+        processor never enter that path at all."""
+        for mm_processor, mm_path_entered in (
+            (_make_mm_processor(False), True),
+            (None, False),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(mm_processor=mm_processor):
+                tm = _make_tm(declares_audio=False)
+                tm.mm_processor = mm_processor
+                sentinel = object()
+                _stub_pipeline_past_guard(tm, sentinel)
+
+                self.assertIs(_run_tokenize(tm, _make_request(["x.wav"])), sentinel)
+                if mm_path_entered:
+                    tm._validate_mm_limits.assert_called_once()
+                else:
+                    tm._validate_mm_limits.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_language_model_only_message_takes_precedence(self):
+        tm = _make_tm()
+        request = _make_request(["x.wav"])
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "--language-model-only"):
+            _run_tokenize(tm, request, language_model_only=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=2)
